articles.title: Accesso Intelligence Adds 100+ AI Decision Skills for Attraction Operators
articles.summary: Accesso Technology Group has expanded its AI-powered decision intelligence platform with a library of over 100 Decision Skills, drawing on 25 years of attractions industry data. The tools are designed to help operators apply AI to everyday operational tasks without requiring prompt engineering expertise. For FEC operators, this lowers the barrier to adopting AI-driven decision-making across staffing, pricing, and guest management.

articles.title: Accesso Expands AI Platform with 100+ Decision Skills for Visitor Attractions
articles.summary: Accesso's Intelligence platform now features over 100 reusable Decision Skills that guide operators through common attraction management tasks using AI. The addition addresses the 'cold start problem' of AI adoption by packaging best practices directly into the platform interface. FEC operators can use these tools to improve consistency across their workforce without needing deep data science knowledge.

articles.title: WhiteWater's Vantage Platform Deployed at 12 US Attractions, Eyes Long-Term Evolution
articles.summary: WhiteWater's Vantage guest technology platform, which unifies ticketing, payments, loyalty, F&B, retail, and access control into a single ecosystem, is now live at 12 US attractions. The company emphasizes ongoing partnership and platform evolution as key to sustaining value beyond initial deployment. For FEC operators evaluating all-in-one guest technology solutions, Vantage's growing install base offers a useful proof-of-concept.

articles.title: Extreme Rush FEC Closes Just Six Months After Opening in Pocatello
articles.summary: Extreme Rush, an indoor entertainment center in Pocatello, Idaho, appears to have shut down only six months after its opening, leaving customers with unused gift cards. The rapid closure highlights the operational and financial risks facing new FEC entrants, particularly in smaller markets. A follow-up report notes that local businesses stepped in to honor affected gift cards, a community-goodwill move worth noting.

articles.title: Local Businesses Honor Unused Gift Cards After Extreme Rush FEC Closes
articles.summary: Following the sudden closure of Extreme Rush in Pocatello, Idaho, two local businesses stepped up to accept the failed venue's unredeemed gift cards. The situation underscores the financial and reputational risks of gift card liability for FEC operators, as well as the community relations opportunity in handling closures responsibly. Operators should review their own gift card policies and financial safeguards in light of this case.

articles.title: How Dream Garden Tailors FEC Builds for Diverse Markets
articles.summary: InPark Magazine profiles Dream Garden, a supplier that customizes family entertainment center concepts and builds for different demographic and regional markets. The piece explores how design, attraction mix, and operational considerations vary significantly depending on the target audience and geography. FEC developers and investors considering new builds or conversions will find the market-differentiation approach particularly relevant.

articles.title: Blue Motion Games Scores Major US Chain Rollout for John Wick Arcade Attraction
articles.summary: Blue Motion Games' motion-based arcade title John Wick: Continental Pursuit, released in June in partnership with Lionsgate, has landed a landmark placement deal with a major US entertainment chain. The Montreal-based developer now has three titles distributed across North America, Europe, Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East. The deal signals growing appetite for IP-driven, motion-based arcade content in FEC and LBE settings.

articles.title: TEA 2025 Attendance Report: World's Top Theme Parks See Flat Visitation
articles.summary: The Themed Entertainment Association's annual attendance index shows visitation to the world's 25 leading theme parks was essentially flat in 2025. For FEC operators, flat big-park attendance can signal opportunity as consumers seek out more accessible and affordable local entertainment options. The report provides a useful macro benchmark for understanding where the broader attractions market stands heading into 2026.

articles.title: Round1 Opens Second Colorado Location at Colorado Mills Mall on Halloween
articles.summary: Japanese arcade and entertainment chain Round1 opened its second Colorado location at Colorado Mills Mall, celebrating with Halloween giveaways. Round1 continues its steady US expansion, bringing its mix of bowling, arcade games, karaoke, and amusements to new markets. The opening is a continued signal of Round1's aggressive US growth strategy and a competitive data point for regional FEC operators.

articles.title: Massive Launch Entertainment Center Opens in Pensacola
articles.summary: A large-format indoor entertainment venue called Launch has opened in Pensacola, Florida, adding to the market's growing FEC footprint. The opening reflects continued consumer demand for indoor entertainment destinations in mid-sized Sun Belt markets. Operators in adjacent markets should monitor how this new entrant performs and what attraction mix it offers.

articles.title: Pensacola's The Pelican Opens as New Indoor Entertainment Complex
articles.summary: A new indoor entertainment complex called The Pelican has opened in Pensacola, offering another competitive option in a market also receiving the Launch FEC. The simultaneous opening of multiple FEC-style venues in the same metro area raises questions about market saturation and differentiation strategy. Operators and investors in secondary markets should take note of this clustering dynamic.

articles.title: Imagicaaworld Sells Hotel, Acquires Water Park Stake, and Targets Indoor Entertainment Growth
articles.summary: Indian attractions operator Imagicaaworld is restructuring its portfolio by divesting its hotel asset, acquiring a stake in a water park, and targeting an indoor entertainment expansion. The strategic pivot reflects a broader trend of attractions companies sharpening their focus on high-throughput, experience-driven venues. FEC suppliers and investors with Asia-Pacific exposure should watch Imagicaaworld's indoor push closely.

articles.title: Dartsee Launches Compact 'Mini' Format to Bring Interactive Darts to Smaller Venues
articles.summary: Dartsee has unveiled the Dartsee Mini, a smaller version of its automated-scoring digital darts system already installed in over 500 venues across 43 countries. The compact unit uses three cameras above a standard dartboard rather than a surrounding ring system, making it viable for venues with limited floor space. FEC and bar-entertainment operators looking for a lower-footprint social gaming addition should evaluate this new format.

articles.title: Hello Park Begins Construction on Two New Locations
articles.summary: Indoor entertainment brand Hello Park has broken ground on two new locations, signaling continued expansion in the family-focused FEC segment. The simultaneous multi-site construction effort suggests strong franchisee or investor confidence in the concept's model. Competing FEC brands and suppliers should track Hello Park's growth trajectory and market positioning.

articles.title: The Game Palacio Opens Its 14th Entertainment Centre
articles.summary: The Game Palacio, a growing entertainment center chain, has opened its 14th location, demonstrating consistent multi-unit expansion momentum. The milestone reflects sustained consumer demand for arcade and entertainment center experiences at the chain level. FEC operators and suppliers should note this brand's scaling approach as a benchmark for multi-unit growth.

articles.title: Paradise Adventures to Bring Game Shows, Beach Play, and More to Midland Mall
articles.summary: Paradise Adventures is set to open a new family entertainment concept inside Midland Mall in Michigan, featuring game shows, beach-themed play areas, and other interactive attractions. The mall-based FEC model continues to attract operators looking to repurpose underutilized retail space. This opening is a useful case study for operators and mall landlords exploring entertainment-led retail conversions.

articles.title: Nostalgia-Driven Investor Revives Local Bowling Alley in Wisconsin
articles.summary: A Wisconsin bowling alley is being reborn thanks to an owner motivated by fond childhood memories of the venue, highlighting the emotional and community-driven factors that often underpin independent FEC investments. The story touches on the challenges and appeal of restoring legacy bowling venues in smaller markets. For the industry, it illustrates the continued cultural resonance of bowling as a community anchor.

articles.title: Time Mission Scottsdale Escape Room Concept Plans 2027 Arizona Opening
articles.summary: Time Mission, an escape room entertainment concept, has announced plans to open a Scottsdale, Arizona location in 2027. The announcement adds to a growing pipeline of escape room and immersive entertainment venues targeting the competitive Phoenix metro market. Operators in the region should factor this new entrant into their competitive planning.

articles.title: WAVE Aquatic Safety Names New Leadership After ACB Safety Products Acquisition
articles.summary: WAVE Aquatic Safety, a maker of drowning detection technology for pools and aquatic facilities, has announced a new leadership team following its acquisition by ACB Safety Products International. The leadership transition marks the next growth phase for the company as it scales its AI-based aquatic safety platform. FEC operators running water attractions or indoor pools should be aware of this evolving safety tech provider.

articles.title: UK Snooker Hall Seeks Planning Approval to Convert to Bowling and Indoor Entertainment Venue
articles.summary: A snooker hall in West Cumbria, England is pursuing plans to transform into a six-lane bowling and indoor entertainment venue. The project illustrates the broader trend of repurposing legacy leisure facilities into modern FEC-style entertainment destinations. UK operators and developers looking at conversion opportunities will find this a relevant model.

articles.title: Gresham Wunderland Drops Movie Theater, Eyes FEC Expansion
articles.summary: Oregon's Gresham Wunderland entertainment center is closing its in-house movie theater and redirecting resources toward expanding its core FEC offerings. The move reflects a broader industry trend of FECs shedding underperforming cinema components in favor of higher-engagement, higher-margin attractions. Operators carrying cinema as part of a mixed-use entertainment concept should take note of this strategic pivot.

articles.title: Complete Sports and Management India Wins Two New FEC Contracts
articles.summary: Indian publicly listed leisure operator Complete Sports and Management (BSE: CSML) has won contracts for two new family entertainment center projects. The wins signal continued FEC investment momentum in the Indian market as disposable income and demand for out-of-home entertainment grow. Suppliers and investors targeting emerging markets in South Asia should track CSML's project pipeline.

articles.title: Dreamland Playground Offers Custom FEC Equipment and Turnkey Project Support
articles.summary: China-based Dreamland Playground supplies commercial indoor playground, trampoline park, and FEC equipment with full project support from design through installation, claiming over 5,000 worldwide projects. All equipment is certified to EN and ASTM safety standards, covering soft play, ninja courses, climbing, and trampoline attractions. FEC operators evaluating equipment sourcing partners for new builds or refurbishments should consider this supplier's full-service capabilities.

articles.title: Winner's Circle FEC in Longmont Marks Two Years with Regional Recognition
articles.summary: Winner's Circle, a family entertainment center in Longmont, Colorado, is celebrating its second anniversary alongside regional industry recognition for its performance and community engagement. The milestone offers a positive benchmark for independent FEC operators navigating the challenging early years of a new venue. Operators can draw lessons from the venue's approach to building local loyalty and earning peer recognition.

articles.title: Henderson Sport & Social Club Brings Laser Tag, Volleyball, and Bar Concept to Las Vegas Suburb
articles.summary: Henderson Sport & Social has opened a new venue in the Las Vegas metro area combining laser tag, recreational volleyball, and a bar into a social entertainment concept targeting adults. The hybrid sports-bar-entertainment model is gaining traction as operators seek to attract a broader age demographic beyond traditional family audiences. FEC operators considering adult-oriented social entertainment additions will find this concept worth studying.

articles.title: 'Masha and the Three Bears' Debuts Location-Based Entertainment in the Middle East
articles.summary: The popular animated IP 'Masha and the Three Bears' has launched its first location-based entertainment experience in the Middle East, expanding the brand's physical presence beyond content. IP-driven LBE activations are a growing revenue stream for content owners and an increasingly popular attraction anchor for FEC operators seeking ready-made audience awareness. Operators in the Middle East and globally should watch how this IP performs in a physical venue context.

articles.title: Tech Failures Expose Operational Vulnerabilities Across the Theme Park Industry
articles.summary: A new report examines how technology outages and system failures are creating operational disruptions at theme parks and attractions, from ticketing breakdowns to ride control system issues. As FECs become increasingly dependent on integrated digital platforms, the lessons from large-park tech failures apply directly to smaller venues. Operators should review their system redundancy and incident response plans in light of these industry-wide vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Why Experience Design Must Be Embedded in Venue Strategy from Day One
articles.summary: An industry analysis argues that experience design fails when it is treated as a late-stage add-on rather than a foundational element of a venue's commercial and physical strategy. The piece calls for bringing creative and experience thinking into masterplanning from the outset to create destinations that drive repeat visitation. FEC developers and operators planning new builds or major renovations will find the framework directly applicable.
